sentences.text: Vescornis is an extinct genus of avialan, a type of bird, belonging to the Enantiornithes clade.
This creature lived during the Barremian to Aptian stages, approximately 125.77 to 119.57 million years ago.

The holotype fossil, which is the specimen the species is based on, is held at the Nanjing Institute of Geology and Paleontology, Chinese Academy of Sciences. The genus was formally described by Zhang and colleagues in 2004.
Vescornis is classified within the family Gobipterygidae.

Fossils were found in Early Cretaceous rocks originally attributed to the Yixian Formation in Hebei Province, China. Later geological studies reclassified the rock formation containing these fossils as the Huajiying Formation.

It is debated whether Vescornis is a synonym of the genera Jibeinia or Hebeiornis. There is no scientific consensus on the synonymy of Vescornis, Jibeinia, and Hebeiornis, with some researchers treating them as distinct species. Researchers conclude that verifying if Vescornis and Jibeinia are the same species is impossible without rediscovering the lost holotype of Jibeinia.
